distinguishing_features: Uses a focused high-intensity ultrasound array to generate cavitation-driven micro-shockwaves rather than passively detecting cavitation through pump impedance changes.
Targets ice nucleation within supercooled droplets at marginal supercooling using on-demand acoustic cavitation.
Uses outside-air temperature as an automatic activation gate for cloud seeding.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to induce ice crystal formation on demand in marginally supercooled cloud droplets when passive ice-nucleating agents have insufficient nucleation efficiency.
parsed.viable_reason: The proposed airborne mechanism is physically implausible as written because an acoustic field in low-pressure air cannot generate liquid cavitation bubbles in dispersed micron-scale cloud droplets at the stated operating conditions, and the cited pressure relation does not establish such droplet-scale nucleation.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying focused ultrasound and inertial-cavitation shockwaves to directly initiate ice nucleation departs non-obviously from the closest prior art's use of cavitation as a monitored pump-flow phenomenon.
